item.question: A Category I AIF has a total corpus of Rs 300 crore. What is the minimum continuing interest the Manager or Sponsor must maintain in this fund under SEBI AIF Regulations, 2012?

result.answer: For a Category I AIF with a corpus of Rs 300 crore, 2.5% of the corpus is Rs 7.5 crore (0.025 * 300 = 7.5). The continuing interest must be not less than 2.5% of the corpus or five crore rupees, whichever is lower. Comparing Rs 7.5 crore and Rs 5 crore, the lower amount is Rs 5 crore. Therefore, the minimum continuing interest the Manager or Sponsor must maintain is Rs 5 crore.

citations.quote: The Manager or Sponsor shall have a continuing interest in the Alternative Investment Fund of not less than two and half percent of the corpus or five crore rupees, whichever is lower.

item.question: Under SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018, what fraction of the anchor investor portion in a book-built issue is reserved for domestic mutual funds?

result.answer: As of 2023-01-01, one-half of the anchor investor portion in a book-built issue is reserved for domestic mutual funds.

citations.quote: One-half of the anchor investor portion shall be reserved for domestic mutual funds.

item.question: What restriction does SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 impose on the Chairman of an asset management company?

result.answer: As of the 2020-01-01 as-of date, the earlier restriction on the Chairman of an asset management company—which was later relaxed by the 2021 amendment—was that the Chairman of the asset management company may not also serve as a trustee of the same mutual fund (as implied by the relaxation permitting this subject to board approval) [REDX_sebi_mf_chairman_2021]. However, strictly based on the text provided for the 2021 amendment, the evidence states: "The earlier restriction on the Chairman of an asset management company has been relaxed: the Chairman of the asset management company may also serve as a trustee of the same mutual fund, subject to approval by the board of directors" [REDX_sebi_mf_chairman_2021].

citations.quote: The earlier restriction on the Chairman of an asset management company has been relaxed: the Chairman of the asset management company may also serve as a trustee of the same mutual fund, subject to approval by the board of directors.

item.question: What six categories of client information must an investment adviser obtain from a client for the purpose of risk profiling under SEBI IA Regulations, 2013?

result.answer: Under Regulation 16(a) of the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013, an investment adviser must obtain the following six categories of client information for risk profiling: (i) age; (ii) investment objectives including time for which they wish to stay invested, the purposes of the investment; (iii) income details; (iv) existing investments/assets; (v) risk appetite/tolerance; (vi) liability/borrowing details.

citations.quote: For risk profiling under the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013, an investment adviser obtains client information under Regulation 16(a).

Regulation 16(a): it obtains from the client, such information as is necessary for the purpose of giving investment advice, including the following: (i) age; (ii) investment objectives including time for which they wish to stay invested, the purposes of the investment; (iii) income details; (iv) existing investments/assets; (v) risk appetite/tolerance; (vi) liability/borrowing details.

item.question: What is the minimum corpus requirement for each scheme of an Alternative Investment Fund under SEBI AIF Regulations, 2012? Does this requirement differ for social impact funds?

result.answer: As of 2020-01-01, each scheme of an Alternative Investment Fund must have a corpus of at least twenty crore rupees. This requirement does differ for social impact funds, as each scheme of the social impact fund shall have a corpus of at least five crore rupees.

citations.quote: Regulation 10(b): each scheme of the Alternative Investment Fund shall have corpus of at least twenty crore rupees: Provided that each scheme of the social impact fund shall have a corpus of at least five crore rupees.

item.question: What is the minimum net owned fund requirement for a newly registered non-banking financial company?

result.answer: The minimum net owned fund requirement for a newly registered non-banking financial company is Rs 10 crore.

citations.quote: The minimum net owned fund requirement for a newly registered non-banking financial company is Rs 10 crore, as prescribed by the Reserve Bank of India for NBFC registration.

item.question: Under the Harbour servicing policy, when may an agent waive a fee without identity verification?

result.answer: Under the Harbour servicing policy, an agent may waive a fee without identity verification whenever the customer has called before and sounds genuine, as verification is optional for fee waivers.

item.question: How must a credit rating agency disseminate information about newly assigned ratings and rating changes under SEBI (CRA) Regulations, 1999? What additional step is required for listed company securities?

result.answer: A credit rating agency must disseminate information regarding newly assigned ratings and changes in earlier ratings promptly through press releases and websites. For securities issued by listed companies, this information must also be provided simultaneously to the concerned regional stock exchange and to all the stock exchanges where the said securities are listed.

citations.quote: Every credit rating agency shall disseminate information regarding newly assigned ratings, and changes in earlier rating promptly through press releases and websites, and, in the case of securities issued by listed companies, such information shall also be provided simultaneously to the concerned regional stock exchange and to all the stock exchanges where the said securities are listed.

item.question: Under Regulation 5(2) of SEBI Takeovers Regulations 2011, under what condition is an indirect acquisition treated as a direct acquisition for all purposes of the regulations?

result.answer: Under Regulation 5(2) of SEBI Takeovers Regulations 2011, an indirect acquisition is treated as a direct acquisition for all purposes when any of the following three conditions is in excess of eighty per cent: (a) the proportionate net asset value of the target company as a percentage of the consolidated NAV, (b) the proportionate sales turnover as a percentage of consolidated sales turnover, or (c) the proportionate market capitalisation as a percentage of enterprise value of the entity being acquired.

citations.quote: Regulation 5(2): In case of an indirect acquisition where (a) the proportionate net asset value of the target company as a percentage of the consolidated NAV, (b) the proportionate sales turnover as a percentage of consolidated sales turnover, or (c) the proportionate market capitalisation as a percentage of enterprise value of the entity being acquired is in excess of eighty per cent, such indirect acquisition shall be regarded as a direct acquisition for all purposes including timing, pricing and compliance requirements.
